why: [4, 4]. 2 is first reached in 7 minutes, then in 3 through 1 and 3. A station's time is final only when it is taken out of the heap, not when it is first reached.

name: 100,000 stations, the end cannot be reached
expr: (lambda r: None if r is None else [r[0], route_cost(args[0], args[1], r[1], args[2], args[3])])(fastest(args[0], list(args[1]), args[2], args[3]))
why: None. The search settles every station it can reach first. Finding the nearest unsettled station by looking through all of them costs O(V) per station, 10¹⁰ steps here; a heap finds it in O(log V) (lesson 3).

name: 2,000 better offers for one busy station
expr: (lambda r: None if r is None else [r[0], route_cost(args[0], args[1], r[1], args[2], args[3])])(fastest(args[0], list(args[1]), args[2], args[3]))
show: station 2001 is offered a better time 2,000 times; it has 100,000 lines out
why: [12001, 12001]. Each better offer pushes a new entry for station 2001, so the heap holds 1,999 old entries for it. An old entry must be skipped when it comes out (its time is more than the station's best). Handling it again reads all 100,000 lines each time: 200 million steps (lesson 3).
